page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The dinner date
title: The dinner date
topic: Language to use in a business proposal
description:
Anna and Tom are at a pizza restaurant for their dinner date, but Anna has work on her mind. She needs to put together a proposal for her new business idea!
This episode focuses on the language to use to make your business proposals really stand out.

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: Would you like to see the menu?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yes please.

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: I was asking the lady actually.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, right.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Anna and Tom are finally on their dinner date at a pizza restaurant. Eating could be difficult for Tom because he's sprained his arm after that accident in the office. He might still have romance on his mind but Anna is thinking about something else. Are you feeling nervous Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Nervous? Why?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Being out on your own with Tom. What are you going to talk about?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Don't worry. I can handle this, besides I want Tom's ideas about developing a new plastic vegetable.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: A plastic vegetable! Oh right. Well, good luck.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So, this is nice. Finally, us together, on our own, me and you, pizza, red wine… expensive red wine, actually.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Lovely, Tom. You know Tom, Paul wants me to develop a new idea – plastic vegetables – I thought, maybe, you might like to help me?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Come on Anna, we're not here to talk business. Tell me about you – the real Anna. Have you had many… err, many boyfriends before?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's a bit personal. What do you think about plastic peas?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Err? Can you not switch off from work for one minute?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom. I think you and me are very similar – we're a good team. If we could come up with a great idea for Paul then who knows… we may get to travel the world selling it together?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, I see. I hadn't thought of it like that. Right well…

transcript.speaker: Waiter
transcript.text: Your pizzas… madam… sir.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. Tom, I think you'll need some help cutting that.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Thanks. Mmm, you smell nice… or is that the pizza?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've got it!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Plastic aubergines!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Plastic aubergines?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Plastic aubergines. They would look great on this table – a sort of decoration.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah! And you could put sauces inside… or salt and pepper. You could be on to something here.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We need to put a proposal together, to give it to Paul. But what should we say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, your proposal needs to be brief but clear. Use positive language to propose your idea to Paul. Use words like 'exceptional', 'fantastic', 'quality', and talk about how it would benefit the business by using words like 'profit', 'efficiency', and 'value for money'. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Are you OK Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Just writing some things down.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: OK, well write down how we could target restaurants and cafes. They'll be begging for our vegetables. Oh this is so exciting… let's drink to our… succ… Oh!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom! What have you done? You've knocked red wine all over me… and my notebook.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ermm, sorry. We had better get you out of that dress.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hmm, what a mess and what a date! But what may be lacking in romance is made up for in a potentially successful business deal. Let's find out how it's going much much later at Tom's flat…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …this exceptional product has fantastic potential…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Say 'demand for this plastic aubergine will reach melting point!' My little joke.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …by making the production more efficient, our customers will get value for money and our profits will increase. There, done.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Great. We can pitch this to Paul first thing on Monday morning. So now, maybe we can get back to our date? Look I saved some of that pizza.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's all cold! Anyway, I had better go. It's late and I want to tidy up this proposal. But it's been great. I can't wait till next time.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Bbbut…Next time?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, that went well! The pizza may be cold but Anna and Tom have developed a red hot proposal. Here's a reminder of some of the words you might want to use to make your business proposal stand out…
Exceptional!
Fantastic!
Quality.
Profit.
Efficiency.
Value for money.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So with the proposal written, Tom and Anna just need to convince Paul – and that means pitching their idea. Find out how they get on next time. Bye for now.
